about.title: Rialto Workplace Injury Claims
about.longDescription: A workplace injury in Rialto rarely comes with a simple answer about who pays. Under California law, workers' compensation is usually your only claim against your employer, and it applies no matter who was at fault. It covers medical care and part of your lost wages, but not pain and suffering. The picture changes when someone other than your employer contributed to the harm. A subcontractor on a job site, the owner of a property you were sent to, the maker of a machine that failed, or another driver who hit your work vehicle on Riverside Avenue or SR-210 can each support a separate third-party claim. Rialto recorded 432 injury collisions in 2025, with reported crashes tending to peak on Fridays between 3 and 5 p.m., and some of those involved people on the clock. LawProactive is a free service, not a law firm. We connect injured Rialto workers with an independent attorney who can sort out which claims apply and who works on contingency, so there is no fee unless there is a recovery.

items.question: I was hit while driving for work on Baseline Road in Rialto. Is workers' comp my only option?
items.answer: Not necessarily. Workers' compensation covers you because you were on the job, but the other driver is a third party, and California law allows a separate injury claim against a negligent third party. That claim can address losses workers' comp does not, such as pain and suffering. An independent attorney can look at the collision report and explain how both paths fit together.

items.question: Can my employer punish me for reporting an injury or filing a claim?
items.answer: No. Retaliating against a worker for reporting an injury or pursuing workers' compensation is illegal in California. You should still report the injury to your employer within 30 days to protect your benefits. If you are being pressured or treated differently after reporting, tell the attorney you are connected with so it can be addressed.

items.question: How long do I have to bring a third-party claim in San Bernardino County?
items.answer: A third-party personal injury claim in California generally must be filed within two years of the injury. That is separate from the 30-day window for reporting the injury to your employer. Because evidence like equipment records and site conditions can change quickly, it helps to speak with an attorney well before the deadline.
